decisions.name: Same-origin BFF instead of a browser Gateway client
decisions.rationale: Keeps Knowledge-Core credentials off the client and lets the UI speak stable DTOs.
tradeoffs: Every authenticated REST call pays a web hop
Cookie and CSRF/origin policy must be maintained in Route Handlers

decisions.name: Gateway remains the only Knowledge-Core edge
decisions.rationale: Web must not reconstruct service topology or bypass typed HTTP contracts.
tradeoffs: Web cannot query service databases for convenience
Contract changes require Knowledge-Core IDL and Gateway mapping first

decisions.name: Standalone Node image on port 3000
decisions.rationale: Matches Next.js production output and keeps probes process-local.
tradeoffs: Two replicas still share no in-process session store beyond cookies
Gateway availability is verified by smoke, not by /api/health

decisions.name: Centralized server-side session layer
decisions.rationale: Cookie handling, refresh rotation, origin checks, retries, and Gateway proxying are maintained in one server-only boundary while Gateway remains the only Knowledge-Core edge.
tradeoffs: Web-facing BFF paths are owned and versioned with the Web application
The Next.js runtime remains required for authenticated browser requests

keyFlows.description: The browser posts to /api/bff/auth/login. The BFF calls Gateway /api/v1/sessions, then sets HttpOnly cookies kc_access and kc_refresh and returns only the user projection.
keyFlows.name: Login and session cookies

keyFlows.description: The browser calls /api/bff/gateway/*. The BFF forwards method, body, and selected tracing headers, attaching the session cookie as the Gateway Authorization header.
keyFlows.name: Authenticated Gateway proxy

keyFlows.description: A 401 from Gateway with a refresh cookie present causes the BFF to call /api/v1/sessions/refresh, rotate cookies, and retry the original request once.
keyFlows.name: Silent refresh

keyFlows.description: Yjs WebSocket traffic goes browser to Collaboration after Knowledge issues a short-lived ticket. The web process does not persist CRDT updates.
keyFlows.name: Live collaboration is not a web-owned hop

principles.description: Access and refresh credentials never enter client JavaScript, localStorage, or the Next.js browser bundle.
principles.name: BFF owns browser sessions

principles.description: Server code reaches Knowledge-Core only through src/lib/api/gateway.ts for server-rendered data and the shared src/lib/bff/gateway.ts for the /api/bff/gateway proxy; pages do not scatter fetch calls.
principles.name: Single Gateway client

principles.description: Mutating BFF routes reject cross-origin requests. Health checks the web process only and does not pretend Gateway is healthy.
principles.name: Fail closed at the origin

principles.description: Folder, document, attachment, and collaboration authority stay in Knowledge-Core services. The UI must not infer permissions.
principles.name: Web does not own backend data

value.purpose: Knowledge-Core-Web is the Knowledge Core product surface: a Next.js App Router UI plus a same-origin BFF. It serves home, Studio, and login shells, localizes Simplified Chinese and English, and keeps Gateway session credentials in HttpOnly cookies. It does not own PostgreSQL, Redis, NATS, object storage, or Yjs persistence; those remain in Knowledge-Core behind the Gateway.

facts.value: Public PR and `main` verification run `.github/workflows/ci.yml` on ARC `hls-standard`. Pushes to `dev` run `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` from `.ci/pipeline.yaml` on ARC: `verify`/`deploy`/`smoke`/`release` use `hls-standard` (non-privileged containers, 8 CPU / 8Gi, min 1 max 4; namespace quota 32 CPU / 32Gi); `package` uses `hls-builder` (privileged Docker-in-Docker 12Gi plus runner 2Gi, both 12 CPU so the pod is 24 CPU / 14Gi, min 0 max 1). Workflow `max-parallel` is 1. The standard namespace is Pod Security privileged only so runners can share hostPath `/var/lib/hls-ci-cache` at `/cache`; GitHub Actions cache is not used. External HTTP(S) uses `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`=`http://10.42.0.1:10991` from the `arc-proxy` Secret; `NO_PROXY` covers localhost, loopbacks, `.svc`, the Kubernetes API, Harbor, Argo, and `.happyladysauce.local`. `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1` remains so Node 24 actions including `create-github-app-token` post honor that proxy. Node/pnpm/Playwright downloads use npmmirror (`cdn.npmmirror.com` / `registry.npmmirror.com`) and do not restore GitHub Actions package caches. Playwright CI `webServer.timeout` is 180s with `PORT=3000` and `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0`. `prewarm-base-images` needs only `plan` so it runs beside `web-verify-build`. `deploy-release` checkouts use `fetch-depth: 0` so `origin/main` ancestry checks succeed. Knowledge-Core-Web/deploy is the editable deployment source and CI synchronizes it automatically to HappyLadySauceM/deploy/Knowledge-Core-Web using the `knowledge-core-web-release` ServiceAccount and in-cluster `https://kubernetes.default.svc:443`; deploy-only changes skip image builds while still validating the overlay, updating GitOps, waiting for Argo, running smoke, and promoting main. Harbor tags candidates by commit SHA, then promotes `:dev` and updates `:previous` after smoke. Failures support rollback, and force-push is forbidden. The `release` environment is limited to `dev` and supplies GH App credentials, kubeconfig, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.

- Web does not own backend data access and must not bypass Gateway.
- Production images use immutable Harbor digests.
- Do not commit plaintext secrets or force-push shared history.
- Gateway routes and network policies are owned by k3s configuration, not this repository.
- `/api/health` checks the web process only; Gateway dependence is verified by smoke.

src/app owns App Router pages, layouts, and BFF route handlers.
src/components owns UI and studio shells.
src/lib owns i18n, the Gateway client, the shared BFF session/proxy layer, and collaboration helpers.
deploy/web owns Kustomize base and overlays.
docker owns the production image.
scripts owns smoke checks.
e2e owns Playwright specs.
docs owns product and technical decisions.
storybook-static, test-results, playwright-report, and .next are generated outputs.

Use strict TypeScript and ESLint. Validate with Vitest, Playwright, production build, and Storybook. Keep Gateway access on the server. Do not put session credentials in client code, cookies readable by JavaScript, or logs.

facts.value: Use Node.js 24.18.1 (CI pin; package engines allow >=20.9.0) and pnpm 10.31.0. Install with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Package tarballs use npmmirror via `.npmrc` (`registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com`). ARC CI (`hls-standard` / `hls-builder` ephemeral pods) downloads Node from `https://cdn.npmmirror.com/binaries/node`, skips GitHub Actions pnpm cache restore, and uses the node-local hostPath cache at `/cache` (`NPM_CONFIG_CACHE`, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, `RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE`). Playwright browsers on ARC CI use `PLAYWRIGHT_DOWNLOAD_HOST=https://cdn.npmmirror.com/binaries/playwright`. Playwright CI `webServer.timeout` is 180s with `PORT=3000` and `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0`. Inject non-secret `KNOWLEDGE_CORE_GATEWAY_URL` for the BFF; the local default is http://localhost:8080. Cluster overlay deploy/web/overlay/dev points at knowledge-core-gateway in namespace knowledge-core-dev. Secrets stay in GitHub or Kubernetes Secrets. The BFF also accepts KNOWLEDGE_CORE_WEB_ORIGIN for exact Origin checks and KNOWLEDGE_CORE_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_MS for the outbound timeout budget.

Inject secrets through GitHub or Kubernetes Secrets only; do not commit plaintext secrets. Authentication cookies are HttpOnly, Secure when the request is HTTPS, and use SameSite Lax for access and Strict for refresh. Logs, metrics, and client bundles must not contain session credentials.

facts.value:
The browser talks only to Knowledge-Core-Web on the same origin. The BFF authenticates through `/api/bff/auth/*` and proxies Gateway HTTP through `/api/bff/gateway/[...path]`. knowledge-core-web depends on knowledge-core-gateway and does not call Identity, Knowledge, Collaboration, Attachment, or Platform directly. Live Yjs traffic is a browser-to-Collaboration path after Knowledge issues a short-lived ticket; the web process does not persist CRDT updates.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Browser --> WebBFF[knowledge-core-web :3000]
  WebBFF --> Gateway[knowledge-core-gateway :8080]
  Gateway --> Identity
  Gateway --> Knowledge
  Gateway --> Collaboration
  Gateway --> Attachment
  Gateway --> Platform
  Browser -.->|Yjs WebSocket after ticket| Collaboration
```
Lint, typecheck, unit tests, production build, e2e, Storybook, Docker build, Kustomize render and server dry-run, Argo sync, and deployment smoke checks pass.
